headline: Meta employees petition against collecting computer-use data for AI model training
summary: The program, called "MCI," collects mouse movements, click locations, keystrokes, and screen content, with no completed privacy reviews provided.
details: Meta employees have launched a petition demanding the company cease collecting their "computer-use" data for training AI models. The program, known as the "Model Capability Initiative" (MCI), gathers extensive human-computer interaction data, including mouse movements, click locations, keystrokes, and screen content.

Concerns have been raised regarding a lack of transparency, as no completed privacy reviews were provided when employees inquired. Furthermore, the outlined privacy mitigations were vague, and executives were afforded a selective opt-out option, which was not extended to all employees.

The petition highlights past privacy incidents at Meta, including a €91 million GDPR fine in 2024 for storing user passwords in plain text. More recently, in March 2026, an AI agent's incorrect instructions led to sensitive user data exposure.

Collecting this data inevitably includes sensitive information like SSNs and protected health information, introducing significant security and regulatory risks. Employee data is protected under acts like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA).

Employees argue that this intrusive, non-consensual data collection contradicts Meta's own Code of Conduct, which emphasizes "Building AI Responsibly" and ensuring AI systems meet legal and regulatory obligations. They believe responsible AI includes respecting individual boundaries and privacy.

The petition calls for a clear commitment that employee computer use data will not be collected for AI training purposes. It asserts that companies should not exploit employees by non-consensually extracting their data for AI development.
